title: Indonesia payments growth slows to 12.6% through 2032
Rupiah Rallies 0.37% as US-Iran Talks Lift Sentiment, BI Holds Rate
article:
Jakarta. Rupiah rallied against the US dollar on Wednesday as progress in US-Iran negotiations, easing concerns over disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz and Bank Indonesia’s decision to hold interest rates supported the Indonesian currency.

The rupiah strengthened 66 points, or 0.37%, to close at Rp 17,818 per dollar on Wednesday (Sept. 23), recovering from Tuesday’s 0.21% decline to Rp 17,884. The dollar index, meanwhile, rose 0.2% to 100.8.

Ibrahim Assuaibi, director of Traze Andalan Futures, said developments in US-Iran relations were among the factors supporting the rupiah. US President Donald Trump said American officials had held a three-hour meeting with Iranian representatives in New York, raising hopes for progress in negotiations.

“Trump described the meeting as very good and productive, raising hopes that negotiations could help ease the conflict and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz,” Ibrahim said on Wednesday.

The meeting marked the first direct contact between US and Iranian officials since June. Iran has also signaled its willingness to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if Washington eases military pressure and lifts its blockade of Iranian ports. However, a final agreement has yet to be secured.

Ibrahim said further support came from Saudi Arabia, which had resumed operations on its East-West oil pipeline, allowing crude shipments to reach the Red Sea port of Yanbu without passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

The pipeline had previously been shut down following a drone attack earlier this month. Despite the positive developments, markets remained cautious as investors assessed the US Federal Reserve’s monetary policy outlook. Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond President Thomas Barkin said inflationary pressures would take time to ease, adding that further interest rate increases might be necessary to bring inflation toward the Fed’s 2% target. Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins also said persistent price pressures called for a more restrictive policy stance to achieve price stability over the long term.

Domestically, Bank Indonesia’s decision to maintain its benchmark interest rate provided another source of support for the rupiah.

At its Sept. 22-23 Board of Governors Meeting, BI kept the BI-Rate unchanged at 5.75%. The Deposit Facility rate remained at 4.75%, while the Lending Facility rate stood at 6.50%.

Ibrahim said the central bank’s decision was aimed at maintaining exchange rate stability while supporting economic growth and controlling inflation.

BI also plans to strengthen measures to encourage foreign capital inflows and deepen the money and foreign exchange markets.

Looking ahead, Ibrahim expects the rupiah to remain volatile on Thursday, with the currency potentially weakening to between Rp 17,810 and Rp 17,860 per dollar.

Other currencies closed at Rp 13,949 per Singapore dollar, Rp 112.88 per Japanese yen, Rp 12,629 per Australian dollar and Rp 20,346 per euro.

title: Foreign Capital Returns to Indonesia, with Inflows Reaching Rp 140.7 Trillion
article:
Jakarta. Indonesia recorded Rp 140.7 trillion ($7.9 billion) in accumulated foreign capital inflows as of Sept. 14, Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara said Wednesday, signaling an improvement after periods of capital outflows earlier this year.

Suahasil said foreign funds had recently begun returning to Indonesian financial assets amid continued turbulence in the global economy.

“A few months ago, we were still seeing capital outflows, but more recently we have begun to see funds coming in,” Suahasil told the ANTARA Business Forum in Jakarta.

The inflows have primarily gone into government securities (SBN) and Bank Indonesia Rupiah Securities (SRBI), he said.

“As of Sept. 14, last week, accumulated capital inflows reached Rp 140.7 trillion through SBN and SRBI,” Suahasil said.

He said the trend indicated improving global investor perceptions of Indonesia despite continued uncertainty in the world economy.

“This is the kind of macroeconomic management that we must maintain,” he said.

The Finance Ministry has also pointed to Indonesia's government bond market as remaining resilient amid global uncertainty, with the yield spread between Indonesian government securities and US Treasuries relatively low compared with several other countries.

Three Fiscal Priorities

 Suahasil also outlined three fiscal strategies aimed at strengthening the state budget.

The first is to optimize state revenue collection and increase Indonesia's tax ratio by improving taxpayer compliance, broadening the tax base and ensuring the effective implementation of the government's Coretax administration system.

The government also plans to continue adapting the tax system to developments in the global and digital economies while maximizing revenue from other sources.

The second priority is improving the quality of government spending.

Suahasil said the state budget must become more efficient and better targeted, while coordination between the central and regional governments should be strengthened through greater policy alignment.

His third priority is developing more innovative financing instruments.

With the state budget designed to remain expansionary, Suahasil said the government must also broaden its financing approaches while preserving fiscal health.

“We are developing various forms of more innovative financing so they can play a role in maintaining the health of the state budget,” he said.

Suahasil, who was appointed finance minister on Sept. 14, has said his leadership will represent continuity rather than a major change in the ministry's fiscal policy direction.

title: Indonesia’s FX Reserves Reach $146.5 Billion in August
article:
Jakarta. Indonesia’s foreign exchange reserves stood at $146.5 billion at the end of August, providing a buffer against external shocks as heightened global uncertainty weighs on emerging markets and pressures the rupiah.

The reserves were equivalent to 5.4 months of imports, or 5.3 months of imports and government external debt repayments, well above the international adequacy standard of around three months of imports, Bank Indonesia (BI) Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti said after the central bank’s September 22-23 Board of Governors Meeting.

“Indonesia’s balance of payments needs to be continuously strengthened to support external resilience amid heightened global uncertainty,” Destry said.

Indonesia’s trade balance returned to a $120 million surplus in July, following a $450 million deficit in June. Foreign portfolio investment also recorded net inflows of $400 million in the third quarter through Sept. 21, supported by the government’s global bond issuance and inflows into government securities.

However, the rupiah weakened 0.78% from the end of August to Rp 17,855 per US dollar on Sept. 22, as global financial uncertainty intensified.

Renewed tensions in the Middle East pushed oil prices as high as $132 per barrel before they fell below $100 on Sept. 22. Meanwhile, the US Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate to 3.75%-4.00% in September, while higher US Treasury yields weighed on investor appetite for emerging-market assets.

BI said it would continue optimizing foreign exchange interventions and expanding incentives to attract foreign investment inflows to support rupiah stability.

“Bank Indonesia and government policy synergy will continue to be strengthened to improve external resilience amid global volatility,” Destry said.

title: Indonesia’s 2027 State Spending to Top $230 Billion
article:
Jakarta. Indonesia plans to spend Rp 4,097 trillion ($229.90 billion) in 2027, its largest state budget expenditure on record, with the government prioritizing human capital development, infrastructure, and public services.

“This is the first time in the history of the Republic of Indonesia that state expenditure has exceeded Rp 4,000 trillion. This is not just a matter of large spending, but also a great responsibility,” Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara said at the Antara Business Forum in Jakarta on Wednesday.

Suahasil said the spending would prioritize human capital development through programs to boost productivity, improve health and education, and strengthen social protection. The government would also invest in supporting services, including infrastructure development and stronger connectivity, to improve human capital quality.

State spending would be carried out in coordination with the Indonesia Investment Management Agency Danantara and other financial sector authorities, he added.

The government has set state expenditure in the 2027 Draft State Budget (RAPBN) at Rp 4,097.2 trillion, up 3.9% from the 2026 outlook. The allocation comprises Rp 3,362.2 trillion in central government spending and Rp 735 trillion in transfers to regional governments.

Central government spending will focus on improving expenditure quality while maintaining public service performance and supporting household purchasing power to ensure sustainable development.

Meanwhile, regional transfers are expected to improve the quality of local government spending and support more equitable and sustainable development.

On the revenue side, the government projects state revenue to reach Rp 3,426 trillion in 2027, a 6.8% increase from the 2026 outlook, equivalent to 12.23% of gross domestic product (GDP).

The projected revenue consists of Rp 2,908 trillion in tax revenue, Rp 517.4 trillion in non-tax state revenue (PNBP) and Rp 0.7 trillion in grants.

Tax revenue comprises Rp 2,591.4 trillion in tax receipts and Rp 316.6 trillion in customs and excise revenue.

Based on the projected revenue and expenditure, the government has set the 2027 budget deficit at Rp 671.2 trillion, or 2.40% of GDP.

title: BI Holds Benchmark Rate at 5.75% in September to Stabilize Rupiah
article:
Jakarta. Bank Indonesia (BI) kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 5.75% on Wednesday, prioritizing rupiah stability as heightened global uncertainty and tighter US monetary policy weigh on emerging markets.

The central bank also maintained its Deposit Facility rate at 4.75% and Lending Facility rate at 6.50%, Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti said after the September 22-23 Board of Governors Meeting (RDG).

“The decision remains consistent with our strategy to stabilize the rupiah amid persistent external pressures, while keeping inflation within target and supporting sustainable economic growth,” Destry said.

Global uncertainty has intensified amid renewed tensions in the Middle East, which pushed oil prices to as high as $132 per barrel before they fell below $100 on Sept. 22. The US Federal Reserve also raised its benchmark rate to 3.75%-4.00% in September, while higher US Treasury yields have weighed on investor appetite for emerging-market assets.

The rupiah stood at Rp 17,855 per US dollar on Sept. 22, weakening 0.78% from the end of August. BI said it would strengthen foreign exchange interventions and expand incentives to attract foreign investment inflows and support currency stability.

Indonesia's economy is projected to grow 4.9%-5.7% this year, supported by government stimulus, improving consumer confidence and investment. Bank lending grew 13.65% year-on-year in August, up from 13.58% in July.

Meanwhile, inflation rose to 3.19% year-on-year in August from 2.88% in July, driven mainly by higher food prices, including chicken, bird's eye chilies and rice. BI expects inflation to remain within its 2.5% ± 1% target in 2026 and 2027.

Foreign exchange reserves stood at $146.5 billion at the end of August, equivalent to 5.4 months of imports.

title: Businesses Back Mandatory Halal Rules, Warn of Rising Compliance Costs
article:
Jakarta. Indonesia’s mandatory halal certification policy, set to take effect on Oct. 18, 2026, has drawn support from businesses, but industry groups are urging the government to simplify procedures and keep compliance costs from driving up production expenses and consumer prices.

Indonesian Employers Association (Apindo) Chairwoman Shinta W. Kamdani said businesses supported the policy as a means of protecting consumers and providing greater certainty. However, its effectiveness would depend on the readiness of the systems and ecosystem supporting its implementation.

“Industry needs four key things: certainty, simplification, harmonization and efficient compliance costs,” Shinta said on Tuesday.

She said the government needed to provide clear, written and consistent technical guidelines and standard operating procedures (SOPs) to prevent differing interpretations among regulators, surveyors, customs officials, businesses and overseas suppliers.

Certification and administrative procedures should also be integrated to eliminate duplication, she said, adding that existing systems, including the Online Single Submission (OSS) platform, should be optimized to prevent businesses from facing overlapping platforms and administrative requirements.

Shinta also called for broader recognition of halal certificates issued by foreign institutions.

For raw materials and products already certified by credible foreign halal institutions recognized by Indonesia, she said, the government should prioritize recognition rather than requiring recertification or repeated verification.

“The broader the recognition network, the easier it will be for Indonesia to connect with global supply chains without compromising the integrity of halal assurance,” she said.

Additional verification, inspections and administrative procedures could increase industries’ compliance costs, affecting not only companies but also lead times, inventory requirements, working capital and product pricing.

Ultimately, businesses could pass the additional costs of doing business on to consumers.

“Halal should create value, not unnecessary costs. Consumer protection must go hand in hand with product availability, affordability and industrial competitiveness,” Shinta said.

Certification as a Competitive Advantage

 Institute for Development of Economics and Finance (Indef) Executive Director Esther Sri Astuti said halal certification could strengthen consumer confidence in products by providing greater assurance of their quality, cleanliness and halal status.

“With halal certification, consumers feel safer and more confident about the quality, cleanliness and halal status of products,” Esther said.

That trust could help micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) strengthen their position amid increasingly intense business competition.

Halal certification could also provide additional value and differentiate products, particularly as consumers have more goods and services to choose from, she said.

Beyond the domestic market, certification could help businesses access wider markets, particularly in countries where consumers have specific halal requirements or preferences. As such, halal certification should not be viewed solely as a government-mandated obligation, but also as part of a broader strategy to improve business competitiveness.

Esther added that compliance with halal regulations could help businesses avoid potential administrative and criminal sanctions by ensuring their products meet prevailing legal requirements.

However, the requirements could pose challenges for MSMEs with limited capital and human resources.

Costs associated with raw material testing, registration and audits could add to the financial burden on small businesses. These expenses could rise further if businesses needed to adjust their supply chains to ensure that all materials met halal requirements.

Government Support Needed for MSMEs

 Administrative requirements also remain a challenge for businesses seeking halal certification, Esther said.

Collecting documents, appointing halal supervisors and undergoing field audits require additional time and resources. For MSMEs with limited staff, these processes could divert attention from core activities such as production and marketing.

Small and traditional businesses unfamiliar with online registration systems, including the SIHALAL platform, could also struggle with the certification process because of limited digital literacy.

Esther said the government needed to strengthen assistance for MSMEs to ensure mandatory halal certification did not become an obstacle to business activities.

Broader access to technical guidance would be one necessary step.

“Technical guidance must be provided so MSMEs can apply for halal certification,” she said.

Such assistance would help businesses understand the certification process, prepare the necessary documents and navigate digital registration systems. With adequate support, she said, mandatory certification could instead become an opportunity for MSMEs to improve their business management and competitiveness.

Shinta, meanwhile, supported import substitution, provided it was implemented realistically and gradually, taking into account the availability, quality, specifications, volume and competitiveness of domestic raw materials.

Import substitution should not be forced when domestic industries are unable to supply materials at competitive prices and quality, she said, warning that doing so could increase production costs and ultimately push up consumer prices.

Shinta urged the government to develop the mandatory halal system around the principle of “high halal assurance with efficient cost of compliance.”

“We need high halal assurance with efficient cost of compliance, so halal becomes a competitive advantage rather than an additional cost disadvantage for Indonesian industries,” she said.

She also called for continued support for MSMEs through self-declare certification mechanisms and targeted government assistance. However, financing schemes should be designed proportionately to avoid creating additional financial obligations for businesses beyond existing requirements.

Ultimately, the success of mandatory halal certification should not be measured solely by the number of certificates issued, Shinta said.

“It should also be measured by its ability to protect consumers, maintain smooth supply chains and affordable prices, and strengthen the competitiveness of Indonesian industries,” she said.

title: Tata Turmoil Shines Light on India Succession Woes
article:
Mumbai. In little over a month, the chairman of India's corporate giant Tata Group has gone from seeking another term to announcing his departure to returning to the role.

The saga around Natarajan Chandrasekaran, who has headed the multi-billion-dollar empire for nearly a decade, has laid bare the succession challenge confronting India's industrial behemoths.

The leadership battle at Tata Group, whose businesses span everything from Jaguar Land Rover cars to Apple iPhone assembly, has highlighted weaknesses in governance and the power struggle between boards and controlling families.

But the consequences extend far beyond shareholders, with a growing number of succession dramas shaking global confidence in India, whose economy relies heavily on corporate giants, analysts say.

The Tata fiasco came to a head last week when the board of Tata Sons, the group's holding company, granted Chandrasekaran another five-year term.

The announcement came despite objections from the Tata Trusts, the philanthropic entities that control the conglomerate and which are chaired by family patriarch Noel Tata.

"The mutiny of the board against the controlling shareholder is possibly a first, and not the right precedent for corporate India," independent advisory firm IiAS said in a note.

Tata is far from an isolated case: from banks to consumer goods, some of India's biggest companies have been rocked by leadership exits and botched handovers in recent months.

"In the last 18-24 months, we've seen a number of CEOs being churned at the top," Navnit Singh of executive search firm Korn Ferry told AFP.

"I do think boards may not be spending enough time looking at long-term succession. Often enough companies do not have a 'hit by the bus' contingency plan and are often caught off guard."

The roots of the Tata conflict run deep.

For much of the year, Chandrasekaran's future hung in the balance as Noel Tata raised concerns about losses at some group companies, investment spending and the possibility of listing Tata Sons.

Leadership Crisis

 The tensions intensified after the death of former patriarch Ratan Tata in 2024, leaving unresolved questions over how authority would be shared within India's largest conglomerate.

"When Ratan was alive, he didn't trust Noel Tata enough to make him the chairman of the Trusts," said Shriram Subramanian of advisory firm InGovern.

"He didn't ensure that there was a structured handover of power even when he was alive."

The bank's chief executive Sashidhar Jagdishan declined another term last month, an abrupt departure that came after the shock resignation of its chairman, forcing directors into a hurried search for new leadership.

At Godrej Consumer Products, chief executive Sudhir Sitapati secured shareholder approval for a second five-year term in August only to resign days later, fuelling speculation about tensions between management and the founding Godrej family.

Experts say such episodes reveal a failure by boards to prepare for leadership transitions before they become crises.

"Independent directors are meant to ask the uncomfortable question, 'who's next, and are they ready?' years before it becomes urgent," said Tulsi Jayakumar, an economics professor specializing in family business.

"Instead, most boards wait for a health scare or a boardroom crisis to even put succession on the agenda. That's not governance, that's crisis management wearing a governance hat."

Ageing Billionaires

 The Tata Group's annual revenues are roughly equivalent to about 5% of India's GDP, and it has become a key investor in strategic sectors including semiconductors, batteries and electronics manufacturing.

"When succession stumbles at a group the size of Tata, it isn't a private family matter; it's a systemic one," Jayakumar said.

Such conglomerates sit at the centre of supply chains, employ hundreds of thousands of people and play an outsized role in shaping investor confidence, she noted.

"A prolonged succession fight signals to global capital that governance in India still runs on personality, not process," she said.

The issue is particularly significant in a country where family-controlled businesses account for most economic activity.

India's ageing billionaires are preparing for one of the biggest intergenerational transfers of wealth globally to their children -- $382 billion according to UBS data -- which implies a massive shake-up in the way many of these empires will be run.

That transition could reshape some of the country's biggest corporate empires and test whether boards are prepared to manage increasingly complex successions.

"Succession planning is under far greater public scrutiny now," said Amit Tandon of IiAS, noting that investors understand that "when the baton is passed to the next generation... it changes the trajectory of the company".

"The best way to look at it is that succession planning is an art, not a science," he added.

"And Indian businesses haven't really cracked it yet."

title: Indonesian Stocks Gain Despite Rupiah, Global Monetary Policy Concerns
article:
Jakarta. Indonesian stocks opened 0.33% higher at 6,297 on Tuesday, as investors awaited Bank Indonesia’s (BI) latest interest rate decision amid concerns over the rupiah’s stability and global monetary policy.

Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) moved in positive territory in early trading, ranging between 6,297 and 6,313.

RTI data shows 641.53 million shares had changed hands in the opening minutes, with a transaction value of Rp 247.34 billion ($13.87 million) and a trading frequency of 50,793 transactions. A total of 293 stocks advanced, 125 declined, and 230 remained unchanged.

Phintraco Sekuritas projected the JCI would test the 6,186-6,200 range, as investors awaited the outcome of BI’s Board of Governors Meeting (RDG), scheduled for Tuesday.

The brokerage expected BI to keep its benchmark interest rate, or BI Rate, unchanged at 5.75%.

The Federal Reserve previously raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 4%, narrowing the spread between the BI Rate and the Federal Funds Rate (FFR) to 1.75 percentage points from 2 percentage points.

Despite the narrowing, Phintraco Sekuritas said the spread remained wider than the average of 0.75-1.25 percentage points recorded over the past three years. The wider differential this year was intended to maintain an attractive interest rate differential for foreign investors while strengthening rupiah stability, the brokerage said.

Phintraco Sekuritas expected BI to consider another rate hike if the rupiah continued to weaken or the Fed resumed its tightening cycle.

However, BI was also expected to continue supporting economic growth, limiting the likelihood of aggressive monetary tightening. Further rate increases could be considered if the rupiah depreciated rapidly or inflation rose above BI’s target.

“Inflationary pressures are also expected to ease again as global oil prices correct. This could give BI room to avoid being too aggressive with its interest rate policy,” Phintraco Sekuritas said.

Beyond the rate decision, investors were also awaiting August 2026 credit growth data, which was projected to accelerate to 15% year-on-year.

Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia said global market sentiment was mixed as investors continued to monitor the Federal Reserve’s policy direction, geopolitical developments in the Middle East and oil price movements.

Statements from Fed officials highlighted concerns over persistent inflationary pressures, keeping investors focused on the outlook for US monetary policy.

Meanwhile, Pluang’s research team said long-term gold prices were driven more by expectations of fiscal deficits than by interest rate levels themselves, with monetary policy serving as a transmission channel rather than the primary driver.

International Monetary Fund (IMF) data showed that the US fiscal deficit was projected to remain above 7% in the coming years, while the global debt-to-GDP ratio had climbed from 82.1% in 2019 to 95.3% this year. The US debt-to-GDP ratio was projected to reach 142% by 2031.

Pluang also pointed to the US Treasury Department’s decision to triple buybacks of long-term bonds to curb yields, describing the move as a bullish signal for gold. The brokerage said the approach would require the government to refinance through short-term debt, which is more vulnerable to market volatility.

“We maintain our gold price target of $5,200 over the next 12 months, viewing the Fed’s hawkish pressure today as a short-term consolidation within a long-term structural trend that remains intact,” Pluang said.

title: Investment Grows More Efficient but Creates Fewer Jobs, Economist Says
article:
Jakarta. Investment in Indonesia has become more efficient at generating economic output over the past two years, but its ability to create jobs has weakened, according to Bank Central Asia (BCA) Chief Economist David Sumual.

David said a declining Incremental Capital Output Ratio (ICOR) indicated that investment was generating more economic growth for each unit of capital deployed.

“Investment continues to grow positively and has become more efficient in driving growth over the past two years, as reflected in the declining ICOR trend,” David said Tuesday.

A lower ICOR generally indicates greater capital efficiency because less additional investment is required to generate an additional unit of economic output.

But David said that improvement has not been matched by investment's capacity to generate employment.

According to his analysis, every $1 million in investment created an average of 26.2 jobs during the 2015–2019 period. That figure fell to 16.5 jobs per $1 million from the fourth quarter of 2024.

The divergence suggests that Indonesia's investment challenge is no longer simply about attracting more capital, David said, but also about ensuring that investment produces broader employment benefits.

Indonesia recorded Rp 1.9312 quadrillion ($108.3 billion) in realized investment in 2025, exceeding the government's full-year target. Investment reached another Rp 1.0106 quadrillion in the first half of 2026, equivalent to 49.5% of the government's Rp 2.0413 quadrillion target for the year.

Official data show that investment realization in the first half of 2026 increased 7.2% year on year and generated 1.45 million direct jobs, up 15% from the corresponding period of 2025.

Job Creation Shows Signs of Recovery

 David said the latest figures nevertheless point to an improvement in investment's employment impact.

In the first half of 2026, every $1 million in investment generated an estimated 25.3 jobs, he said, a significant recovery from the previous level of 16.5.

The improvement suggests that the decline in investment-related job creation is not necessarily permanent, although it remains to be seen whether the rebound can be sustained.

David said Indonesia's economic growth has also accelerated over the past two years, supported by public-sector spending and private-sector participation in the government's priority programs.

At the sectoral level, he said growth has been concentrated in industries benefiting from government programs, including agriculture, food and beverages, trade and construction.

“Unfortunately, this concentrated pattern means the benefits of growth are not being enjoyed broadly across society, particularly in terms of job creation,” David said.

title: Two Years into Prabowo Presidency, Economists Question Quality of Economic Growth
article:
Jakarta. Nearly two years into President Prabowo Subianto's administration, Indonesia's economy is growing at a faster pace, but economists say the expansion has yet to translate sufficiently into higher-quality jobs and stronger household purchasing power.

Indonesia's economy grew 5.11% in 2025, accelerating from 5.03% in 2024, according to the Central Statistics Agency (BPS). Growth strengthened further to 5.45% in the first half of 2026, including 5.29% year on year in the second quarter.

However, Center of Reform on Economics (CORE) Indonesia Executive Director Mohammad Faisal said the stronger headline growth had not been accompanied by a sufficiently significant improvement in the quality of employment.

He pointed to Indonesia's labor structure, where informal employment continues to account for the majority of jobs, affecting wages and ultimately household purchasing power.

“Most workers, or 59%, are still employed in the informal sector,” Faisal said.

“This also affects wage levels and ultimately purchasing power, which is why we continue to see a shrinking middle class whose purchasing power has yet to recover,” he added.

Official employment figures illustrate the challenge. BPS recorded 147.67 million employed people in February 2026, an increase of around 1.90 million from a year earlier. However, informal workers increased to 87.74 million from 86.58 million, while formal employment rose to 59.93 million from 59.19 million.

The average monthly wage for employees stood at Rp 3.29 million in February.

Prabowo, who took office in October 2024, has set an ambition of lifting Indonesia's economic growth to as high as 8%.

Faisal said the economy had shown some acceleration during Prabowo's first two years in office, but its current trajectory remained well below that ambition.

“If we look at the achievements over the past two years, there has indeed been some acceleration, but we are still far from the ambition of growth above 6% and eventually 8%,” Faisal said.

Growth above 5% ‘Not Enough’

 Achmad Nur Hidayat, an economist at Universitas Pembangunan Nasional Veteran Jakarta, similarly said Indonesia had maintained economic stability during nearly two years of the Prabowo administration but had yet to achieve the acceleration required to approach 8% growth.

He argued that maintaining growth slightly above 5% should not in itself be considered a major achievement.

“The much more important question is whether that growth is strong enough to take Indonesia toward the 8% target, create quality jobs, increase people's incomes and generate economic momentum across the regions,” Achmad said.

“After nearly two years, the government's challenge is no longer simply to keep the economy growing at around 5%. The government needs to explain where the additional nearly three percentage points of growth will come from over the next three years,” he added.

Achmad, however, pointed to investment as one area where the government had delivered stronger results.

Indonesia recorded Rp 1.93 quadrillion ($108.3 billion) in realized investment in 2025, exceeding the government's target. In the first half of 2026, investment reached Rp 1.01 quadrillion, equivalent to 49.5% of the full-year target of Rp 2.04 quadrillion.

Investment associated with downstream processing reached Rp 300.1 trillion in the first half of 2026, accounting for nearly 30% of total investment.

“This is a positive development. Indonesia should not continue indefinitely to export raw materials,” Achmad said.

He cautioned, however, that investment performance should not be judged solely by the amount of capital entering the economy.

The government, he said, should also assess how much investment translates into quality employment and higher worker incomes.

Official Investment Ministry data show that realized investment in the first half of 2026 was associated with nearly 1.45 million direct jobs.

Achmad also pointed to Prabowo's campaign-era pledge to create 19 million jobs, arguing that the government should provide more detailed information allowing the public to assess progress not only by the number of jobs created but also by their quality.

“The government needs to publish an official dashboard explaining how many genuinely new jobs have been created, how many are in the formal sector, how many provide decent wages and which sectors are creating them,” he said.

Such transparency, Achmad said, would make it easier to assess whether Indonesia's rising investment is translating into better employment opportunities and improvements in workers' welfare.

IHSG Menguat 1,56%, Cek Proyeksi Pergerakan IHSG pada Kamis (24/9)
article:
Reporter:Shabrina Almaira| Editor:Tri Sulistiowati

KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA.Indeks Harga Saham Gabungan (IHSG) menguat 1,56% pada perdagangan Rabu (23/9/2026) setelah Bank Indonesia mempertahankan BI-Rate di level 5,75%. IHSG ditutup naik 97,87 poin ke level 6.374,91.

Analis Herditya menilai keputusan BI mempertahankan BI-Rate sesuai ekspektasi pasar sehingga sentimen tersebut cenderungpriced-in.

"Mayoritas pergerakan bursa regional Asia bergerak menguat, demikian pula nilai tukar Rupiah yang bergerak menguat terhadap USD," ujar Herditya dalam keterangannya.

Ia memperkirakan IHSG pada perdagangan Kamis (24/9) berpotensi mengalami koreksi terbatas, pada area support 6.355 dan resistance 6.387. Menurutnya, aksi profit taking berpeluang terjadi setelah indeks menguat 1,56% pada perdagangan Rabu.

Sementara itu, Hendra melihat IHSG masih memiliki peluang melanjutkantechnical rebound. Ia menempatkan level 6.463 sebagai resistance penting dalam jangka pendek.

Menurutnya, jika level tersebut mampu ditembus dengan dukungan volume dan perbaikan breadthpasar, IHSG berpeluang bergerak menuju 6.586. Sebaliknya, apabila gagal melewati 6.463, IHSG berpotensi kembali berkonsolidasi dengan support berikutnya di area 6.000-6.035.

Hendra menilai keputusan BI mempertahankan BI-Rate 5,75% memberikan kepastian bagi pasar. Namun, penguatan IHSG hari ini belum sepenuhnya mencerminkan perubahan arus dana asing. Investor asing masih mencatatkan net sell sekitar Rp408 miliar pada perdagangan Rabu, sementara secarayear to date net selldi pasar reguler mencapai sekitar Rp102,9 triliun. Kondisi tersebut menjadi salah satu faktor yang perlu dicermati investor dalam melihat keberlanjutan penguatan IHSG.

title: IHSG Menguat Setelah BI Tahan Suku Bunga, Ini Saham Pilihan Analis
article:
Reporter:Yasmine Awalia| Editor:Handoyo

KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA. Indeks Harga Saham Gabungan (IHSG) menguat signifikan pada perdagangan Rabu (23/9/2026), setelah Bank Indonesia (BI) memutuskan mempertahankan suku bunga acuan atau BI-Rate di level 5,75%.

Pada akhir perdagangan Rabu (23/9/2026), IHSG ditutup naik 97,87 poin atau 1,56% ke level 6.374,91. Penguatan tersebut terjadi setelah pasar memperoleh kepastian mengenai keputusan suku bunga BI dalam Rapat Dewan Gubernur (RDG) yang berlangsung pada 22-23 September 2026.

Melalui siaran pers pada Rabu (23/9/2026), BI mengumumkan mempertahankan BI-Rate sebesar 5,75%, Deposit Facility 4,75% dan Lending Facility 6,50%.

Keputusan tersebut diarahkan untuk menjaga stabilitas nilai tukar rupiah di tengah tekanan eksternal sekaligus tetap mendukung pertumbuhan ekonomi nasional.

Analis menilai keputusan BI memberikan kepastian bagi pelaku pasar sehingga IHSG masih memiliki peluang melanjutkan technical rebound dalam jangka pendek.

Praktisi pasar modal sekaligus Founder Republik Investor Hendra Wardana mengatakan, penguatan IHSG hari ini menunjukkan perbaikan sentimen setelah ketidakpastian keputusan BI mereda. Namun, penguatan tersebut belum sepenuhnya didukung perubahan arus dana asing.

Investor asing masih mencatatkan net sell sekitar Rp408 miliar, sementara secara year to date net sell di pasar reguler mencapai sekitar Rp102,9 triliun.

“IHSG masih memiliki peluang melanjutkan technical rebound dengan level 6.463 sebagai resistance penting. Jika level tersebut berhasil ditembus dengan dukungan volume dan diikuti perbaikan breadth pasar, peluang bergerak menuju area 6.586 semakin terbuka,” ujar Hendra dalam wawancara tertulis dengan Kontan.

Sebaliknya, apabila IHSG gagal melewati level 6.463, indeks berpotensi kembali berkonsolidasi dengan support berikutnya di area 6.000-6.035.

Hendra menilai pergerakan IHSG hingga akhir tahun masih berpotensi berlangsung volatil dan bertahap. Sejumlah faktor yang perlu dicermati antara lain pergerakan rupiah, arus modal asing, suku bunga global serta kondisi geopolitik.Ruang Pelonggaran BI Terbatas

Ruang pelonggaran kebijakan moneter BI juga dinilai semakin terbatas setelah The Federal Reserve menaikkan suku bunga acuan sebesar 25 basis poin menjadi 3,75%-4% pada September.

Apabila BI pada akhirnya menaikkan suku bunga, dampaknya terhadap IHSG berpotensi terasa melalui kenaikan biaya dana, tekanan terhadap valuasi saham serta pergeseran sebagian investor ke instrumen pendapatan tetap.

Sektor yang sensitif terhadap perubahan suku bunga, seperti properti, konstruksi dan consumer discretionary, berpotensi menghadapi tekanan lebih besar.

Sementara itu, sektor perbankan dapat memperoleh sentimen yang berbeda-beda, bergantung pada kualitas aset, likuiditas dan kemampuan masing-masing emiten dalam menjaga margin.

Di sisi lain, Senior Market Analyst Mirae Asset Sekuritas Nafan Aji Gusta melihat apabila IHSG melanjutkan penguatan, sejumlah sektor seperti perbankan, barang konsumen, infrastruktur, komoditas dan energi berpotensi menjadi penopang.

Sektor energi dan barang baku masih memperoleh dukungan dari harga komoditas serta prospek permintaan global.Rekomendasi Saham BNGA, BRMS, SRTG dan INDY

Untuk pilihan saham, Hendra mencermati sejumlah emiten, yakni PT Bank CIMB Niaga Tbk (BNGA), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS), PT Saratoga Investama Sedaya Tbk (SRTG) dan PT Indika Energy Tbk (INDY).

BNGA dinilai dapat memperoleh sentimen dari stabilnya suku bunga domestik. Sementara BRMS dikaitkan dengan katalis dari pergerakan harga emas.

Adapun SRTG dinilai memiliki eksposur terhadap sejumlah aset dan sektor strategis. Sementara INDY masih memperoleh sentimen dari perkembangan sektor komoditas.

title: Rupiah Berpeluang Menguat Kamis (24/9), Ini Pemicunya
article:
Reporter:Vatrischa Putri Nur| Editor:Handoyo

KONTAN.CO.ID – JAKARTA. Nilai tukar rupiah diperkirakan masih memiliki ruang untuk menguat terhadap dolar Amerika Serikat (AS) pada perdagangan Kamis (24/9/2026). Namun, penguatan tersebut berpotensi terbatas seiring pasar mulai mengantisipasi pergerakan dolar AS dan mencermati sentimen global.

Melansir Bloomberg, rupiah spot ditutup pada level Rp 17.818 per dolar Amerika Serikat (AS) pada akhir perdagangan Rabu (23/9/2026), menguat 0,37% dari sehari sebelumnya yang ada di Rp 17.884 per dolar AS.

Pergerakan rupiah di Jisdor BI sejalan dengan rupiah spot. Di pasar spot, rupiah ditutup pada level Rp 17.803 per dolar Amerika Serikat (AS) pada akhir perdagangan Rabu, menguat 0,45% dari sehari sebelumnya yang ada di Rp 17.883 per dolar AS.

Analis mata uang dan founder Traderindo.com, Wahyu Laksono, mengatakan, penguatan rupiah pada perdagangan Rabu (23/9/2026) ditopang oleh sejumlah sentimen, baik dari eksternal maupun domestik.

Dari sisi eksternal, pasar global mencermati sinyal pelonggaran moneter lanjutan di sejumlah negara maju. Kondisi tersebut memicu sedikit aksi risk-on dan aliran modal masuk dalam jangka pendek.

Sementara dari dalam negeri, sentimen utama berasal dari keputusan RDG BI yang mempertahankan BI-Rate di level 5,75%. Menurut Wahyu, keputusan tersebut memberikan sinyal stabilitas kepada pelaku pasar.

Sikap tersebut juga menegaskan komitmen BI dalam menjaga daya tarik imbal hasil aset keuangan domestik, seperti Sekuritas Rupiah Bank Indonesia (SRBI) dan Surat Berharga Negara (SBN), serta kesiapan melakukan intervensi melalui kebijakan triple intervention di pasar spot, DNDF dan SBN di pasar sekunder.

“Dalam jangka pendek, hasil RDG ini menjadi penahan volatilitas yang efektif (cushion), mencegah pelemahan berlanjut menembus level psikologis Rp18.000 dan memicu aksi technical rebound harian,” jelas Wahyu kepada Kontan, Rabu (23/9/2026).

Meski demikian, Wahyu menilai ruang penguatan rupiah pada perdagangan Kamis (24/9/2026) masih terbuka, tetapi lajunya berpotensi terbatas dan cenderung konsolidatif.

Penguatan rupiah sekitar 0,50% secara intraday pada perdagangan Rabu dinilai sebagian telah mencerminkan penyesuaian posisi (pricing in) setelah keputusan suku bunga BI.

Pada perdagangan Kamis, keberlanjutan momentum penguatan rupiah akan sangat bergantung pada apakah pelemahan dolar AS pada perdagangan global malam ini dapat bertahan.

“Penguatan lebih lanjut kemungkinan besar akan tertahan di sekitar area support teknikal USD/IDR sebelum pasar kembali bergerak menyamping (sideways),” kata Wahyu.

Ia menjelaskan, secara teknikal, pergerakan USD/IDR pada grafik harian dan bulanan masih berada dalam struktur higher low.

Wahyu memproyeksikan rupiah pada perdagangan Kamis (24/9/2026) akan bergerak dalam rentang Rp 17.700-Rp 17.900 per dolar AS.

title: Wall Street Dibuka Turun Rabu (23/9), Harga Minyak dan Yield Obligasi Naik
article:
Sumber:Reuters| Editor:Yudho Winarto

KONTAN.CO.ID -Bursa saham Amerika Serikat (AS) dibuka melemah pada perdagangan Rabu (23/9/2026), tertekan kenaikan harga minyak mentah dan imbal hasil (yield) obligasi pemerintah AS.

Investor juga mencermati perkembangan negosiasi untuk mengakhiri konflik di Timur Tengah serta pertemuan penting Presiden AS Donald Trump dengan Presiden China Xi Jinping.

MelansirReuterspada pembukaan perdagangan, Dow Jones Industrial Average turun 92,3 poin atau 0,18% menjadi 51.771,41.

Indeks S&P 500 melemah 2,7 poin atau 0,03% ke 7.761,94, sedangkan Nasdaq Composite turun 30,8 poin atau 0,11% menjadi 27.213,519.

Harga minyak Brent naik lebih dari 1% setelah sebelumnya mencatat penurunan selama lima sesi berturut-turut. Meski demikian, harga minyak masih berada di sekitar level terendah dalam dua pekan.

Kenaikan yield obligasi pemerintah AS tenor dua tahun dan 10 tahun turut membebani sentimen pasar. Investor kembali mengkhawatirkan biaya pinjaman yang akan bertahan tinggi dalam waktu lebih lama.

"Pasar saat ini sedang dalam ketidakpastian... karena imbal hasil obligasi dan harga minyak sedang naik," kata Sam Stovall, chief investment strategist CFRA Research.

Pelaku pasar juga menunggu perkembangan dari pembicaraan antara pejabat AS dan Iran. Negosiasi melalui mediator dimulai pada Selasa (22/9) di sela-sela Sidang Umum Perserikatan Bangsa-Bangsa (PBB).

Dari sisi geopolitik, kedatangan Xi Jinping ke Washington juga menjadi perhatian investor.

Dalam kunjungan kenegaraan tersebut, Xi dijadwalkan bertemu Trump untuk membahas sejumlah isu, termasuk perpanjangan gencatan dagang yang disepakati kedua negara tahun lalu, regulasi kecerdasan buatan (AI), serta penjualan senjata AS ke Taiwan.

Xi juga dijadwalkan bertemu sejumlah pimpinan perusahaan besar AS, termasuk General Motors, Meta, Apple, Amazon dan Tesla.

Saham perusahaan-perusahaan tersebut bergerak datar hingga sedikit menguat dalam perdagangan sebelum pembukaan.

Sementara itu, optimisme terhadap prospek AI masih menjadi salah satu penopang pasar saham AS. Nasdaq pada Selasa (22/9) mencatat rekor tertinggi intraday pertama sejak awal Juni.

Kenaikan tersebut antara lain didorong respons positif pasar terhadap asisten AI Muse milik Meta.

Sejumlah analis menilai perkembangan tersebut berpotensi meningkatkan permintaan terhadap infrastruktur teknologi, sekaligus memunculkan kembali kekhawatiran mengenai potensi disrupsi AI terhadap sejumlah sektor.

Di sisi lain, sektor keuangan S&P 500 mencatat penurunan harian terbesar sejak Maret pada perdagangan sebelumnya.

Saham JPMorgan Chase dan Charles Schwab serta perusahaan yang berorientasi konsumen seperti Uber dan Airbnb bergerak sedikit menguat pada perdagangan sebelum pembukaan, setelah mengalami tekanan tajam sehari sebelumnya.

Dari sisi korporasi, saham jaringan restoran kasual Cracker Barrel naik 6,8% setelah mencatat penjualan kuartal IV yang melampaui estimasi pasar.

Kenaikan belanja AI dan biaya energi yang lebih tinggi akibat perang AS-Iran juga menjadi perhatian Federal Reserve (The Fed).

Pejabat The Fed mengisyaratkan perlunya mempertahankan kebijakan suku bunga ketat lebih lama setelah bank sentral AS menaikkan suku bunga pada pekan lalu.

Pelaku pasar selanjutnya menantikan data Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) AS dari S&P Global untuk September yang akan dirilis pada Rabu. Ekonom yang disurvei Reuters memperkirakan aktivitas bisnis masih berada di zona ekspansi, yakni di atas level 50.

Gubernur The Fed Michael Barr juga dijadwalkan menyampaikan pidato. Pernyataannya akan dicermati investor untuk mencari petunjuk mengenai arah kebijakan moneter berikutnya.

Berdasarkan CME Group FedWatch Tool, pasar kini memperkirakan peluang sekitar 50% bahwa The Fed akan menaikkan suku bunga sedikitnya 25 basis poin pada bulan depan.

title: Begini Arah Pasar Saham Usai Bank Indonesia Pertahankan Suku Bunga 5,75%
article:
Reporter:Rashif Usman| Editor:Ignatia Maria Sri Sayekti

KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA.Bank Indonesia kembali memutuskan menahan suku bunga acuan (BI Rate) di level 5,75% dalam Rapat Dewan Gubernur (RDG) yang berlangsung pada 22-23 September 2026.

Keputusan ini menjadi salah satu katalis yang diperhatikan pelaku pasar saham. Sebab, kebijakan moneter tersebut akan membawa pergerakan Indeks Harga Saham Gabungan (IHSG) baik dalam jangka pendek hingga panjang.

Equity Research Analyst Phintraco Sekuritas, Alrich Paskalis Tambolang mengatakan keputusan BI mempertahankan BI Rate di 5,75% cenderung menjadi katalis stabilisasi, bukan katalis bullish yang kuat.

Pasar sebelumnya sudah mengantisipasi keputusan tersebut, sehingga ruang penguatan IHSG tetap akan sangat bergantung pada stabilitas rupiah, arah yield global, sertaforeign flow.

Di sisi domestik, BI masih memiliki kebijakan makroprudensial yang cukup akomodatif untuk menjaga likuiditas dan mendorong kredit. Pertumbuhan kredit perbankan sendiri masih berada di level dua digit, sehingga transmisi kebijakan ke sektor riil tetap menjadi katalis positif.

“Namun, dalam jangka pendek pasar masih berada dalam fasehigh volatility. Penahanan BI Rate belum cukup menjadi game changer apabila tekanan rupiah dan sentimen eksternal masih berlanjut,” kata Alrich kepada Kontan, Rabu (23/9/2026).

Sementara itu,Head of ResearchPT Mirae Asset Sekuritas Indonesia, Rully Arya Wisnubroto menilai keputusan ini bersifat netral hingga positif bagi pasar saham, mengingat langkah tersebut sudah banyak diantisipasi oleh pelaku pasar sehingga tidak menjadi katalis baru yang signifikan bagi pergerakan IHSG.

Secara terpisah, Financial Educator Manager Sucor Sekuritas, Hendry Wijaya menerangkan keputusan menahan BI Rate ini sudah terpriced-in, di mana mayoritas ekonom memang memprediksi BI mempertahankan rate di 5,75% pada RDG September 2026, sehingga dampak kejutan minim.

Meski keputusan BI sejalan dengan ekspektasi, Hendry menyoroti adanya tekanan dari sisi eksternal yang berpotensi menahan penguatan lanjutan pasar keuangan domestik. Pemicunya adalah langkah bank sentral Amerika Serikat atau The Federal Reserve (The Fed), yang justru menaikkan suku bunga acuannya ke kisaran 3,75%-4,00% pada 16 September 2026.

Kondisi ini, menurut Hendry, membuat risiko kenaikan BI Rate sebesar 25 basis poin menuju 6,00% pada akhir tahun 2026 dinilai meningkat signifikan, terutama jika The Fed kembali menaikkan suku bunga pada pertemuan-pertemuan berikutnya.

"Dalam kesimpulannya pasar cenderung sideways to negatif jangka pendek. Pasar akan bergerak konsolidasi, arus keluar asing berlanjut, baru berpotensi rebound solid jika The Fed tahan kenaikan bunga dan rupiah lebih stabil," tambah Hendry.

Spread Suku Bunga BI - The Fed

Disamping itu, Rully mengingatkan bahwa penyempitan selisih suku bunga atauinterest-rate differentialantara Indonesia dan Amerika Serikat perlu dicermati, terutama setelah The Fed kembali menaikkan suku bunga acuannya sementara BI memilih menahan di 5,75%. Kondisi ini membuat daya tarikcarrypada aset rupiah relatif berkurang dibandingkan periode sebelumnya.

Meski demikian, menurutnya penyempitan spread tersebut tidak serta-merta memicu keluarnya dana asing dari pasar saham. Ia menjelaskan bahwainterest-rate differentialmemiliki dampak transmisi yang lebih langsung terhadap pasar obligasi dan nilai tukar, ketimbang pasar saham.

Bagi investor asing di pasar ekuitas, keputusan investasi lebih banyak dipengaruhi oleh sejumlah faktor lain, seperti prospek pertumbuhan laba, valuasi saham, pergerakan nilai tukar rupiah, premi risiko sovereign, serta selera global risk appetite.

Dalam skenario dasar, Mirae Asset Sekuritas memperkirakan BI Rate akan tetap berada di 5,75%. Ini didasarkan pada langkah pengetatan moneter yang telah dilakukan BI lebih awal ataufront-loaded tighteningsebesar total 100 basis poin pada periode Mei–Juni, di tengah tekanan inflasi domestik yang sejauh ini masih relatif terjaga. Kondisi ini, menurut Rully, memberi BI ruang untuk mempertahankan suku bunga sekaligus mengandalkan stabilisasi nilai tukar sebagai lini pertahanan pertama.

Namun demikian, pihaknya tidak menutup kemungkinan adanya satu kali kenaikan lanjutan sebesar 25 basis poin menjadi 6,00%. Risiko kenaikan tersebut disebut akan meningkat apabila The Fed kembali menaikkan suku bunga, sehingga spread suku bunga Indonesia-AS semakin menyempit, dan pada saat bersamaan tekanan terhadap Rupiah berlangsung lebih persisten.

"Jadi menurut kami, keputusan BI berikutnya akan lebih banyak ditentukan oleh perkembangan nilai tukar dan kondisi eksternal daripada tekanan inflasi domestik semata," ujar Rully.

Proyeksi IHSG Jangka Pendek- Panjang

Alrich memproyeksikan level IHSG pasca putusan suku bunga acuan BI. Untuk jangka pendek, IHSG masih berpotensi bergerak di kisaran 6.186–6.500. Level support berada di level 6.186–6.200 dan resistance 6.500

Untuk jangka menengah, apabila IHSG mampu kembali reclaim 6.500 dan breakout 6.700, peluang technical recovery menuju 6.800–7.000 terbuka.

Sementara untuk jangka panjang, area 7.200–7.500 masih memungkinkan dicapai apabila tekananforeign outflowmereda, rupiah stabil, dan earnings emiten kembali menunjukkan perbaikan.

Namun level tersebut sangat bergantung pada kondisi makro dan arus dana asing, sehingga belum menjadi base case dalam jangka pendek.

Senior Technical Analyst Sucor Sekuritas, Reyhan Pratama juga memproyeksikan IHSG untuk jangka pendek ada potensi rebound dengan resistance yang perlu diperhatikan di 6.371 dan 6.451, lalu support IHSG terdekat di 6.186-6.230, serta resistance jangka menengah di 6.589 dan 6.712

Saham Terdampak Suku Bunga

Alrich mengungkapkan dampak paling langsung dari putusan suku bunga saat ini ialah sektor perbankan, properti, konstruksi, otomotif dan consumer discretionary.

Untuk perbankan, BI Rate yang ditahan memberikan kepastian terhadap cost of fund, meskipun transmisi ke bunga kredit tetap berlangsung bertahap.

Dengan likuiditas yang tetap dijaga dan Kebijakan Insentif Likuiditas Makroprudensial (KLM) diarahkan ke sektor-sektor produktif, bank dengan pertumbuhan kredit dan kualitas aset yang baik masih memiliki ruang untuk mencatat pertumbuhan earnings.

“BBRI, BMRI dan BBCA masih relevan dicermati dari sektor perbankan,” tambah Alrich.

Untuk properti dan konstruksi, stabilnya suku bunga membantu menjagaaffordabilitydan cost offinancing. Sementara pada otomotif, dampaknya lebih bersifat tidak langsung melalui daya beli dan biaya pembiayaan kendaraan.

Dalam kondisi market yang masih volatile, Alrich merekomendasikan sejumlah saham yang dapat dicermati antara lain BBRI, BMRI dan BBCA di target harga masing-masing Rp 3.430, Rp 4.500 dan Rp 6.800 per saham.

Adapun Reyhan menyarankan pelaku pasar untuk mencermati saham BUMI dengan target Rp 212 dan Rp 268, ENRG dengan target di Rp 1.400 dan Rp 1.900, TPIA juga menarik jika breakout Rp 1.900 dengan target di Rp 2.060 dan Rp 2.280 per saham.

title: Berburu Dividen Jelang Cum Date, Ini yang Perlu Dicermati
article:
Penulis:Muhammad Alief Andri| Editor:Tri Sulistiowati

KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA.Sejumlah emiten akan membagikan dividen pada akhir September hingga Oktober 2026. Investor pun perlu mencermati strategi untuk mengejar dividen sekaligus mengantisipasi risiko penurunan harga saham setelah memasuki periode ex-dividend.

Beberapa emiten yang akan membagikan dividen antara lain PT Resource Alam Indonesia Tbk (KKGI), PT Hexindo Adiperkasa Tbk (HEXA), PT Victoria Investama Tbk (VICO), PT Indonesia Fibreboard Industry Tbk (IFII), PT Baramulti Suksessarana Tbk (BSSR), dan PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA).

Senior Market Analyst Mirae Asset Sekuritas, Nafan Aji Gusta, mengatakan investor perlu memahami bahwa dividend yield bukan berarti return yang pasti diterima. Secara teoritis, harga saham akan menyesuaikan turun sebesar nilai dividen pada ex-date.

Namun, penurunan harga aktual bisa berbeda karena dipengaruhi sentimen pasar, likuiditas, kondisi IHSG, serta ekspektasi investor terhadap prospek emiten.

"Risiko dividend trap muncul ketika investor membeli saham hanya karena yield terlihat tinggi, tetapi setelah ex-date harga mengalami koreksi lebih dalam daripada nilai dividen sehingga capital loss menggerus bahkan melebihi pendapatan dividen," ujar Nafan kepada Kontan, Rabu (23/9/2026).

Menurut dia, investor perlu mencermati sejumlah indikator sebelum membeli saham untuk mengejar dividen. Di antaranya payout ratio, arus kas, laba yang mendasari pembagian dividen, rekam jejak pembagian dividen, serta apakah dividen tersebut bersifat rutin atau hanya interim maupun khusus.

Investor juga disarankan tidak sekadar membeli saham pada hari terakhir cum date. Nafan menyarankan investor melakukan akumulasi secara bertahap apabila valuasi dan fundamental emiten memang mendukung.

Investor juga perlu menghitung total return yang merupakan dividen diterima dikurangi potensi capital loss setelah ex-date. Dengan demikian, saham dengan dividend yield tinggi belum tentu memberikan total return yang tinggi.

Untuk investor jangka pendek, disiplin terhadap level support dan batas risiko menjadi penting. Sementara investor jangka menengah hingga panjang dapat lebih berfokus pada kemampuan emiten menghasilkan laba dan arus kas secara berkelanjutan setelah distribusi dividen.

"Dalam konteks ini, pembagian dividen sebaiknya dipandang sebagai bagian dari total return, bukan sebagai alasan tunggal untuk membeli saham," kata Nafan.

Dari sisi fundamental, Nafan melihat BSSR masih ditopang kinerja yang cukup solid. Pada semester I 2026, pendapatan BSSR tumbuh 17,2% menjadi sekitar Rp6,21 triliun dan laba bersih naik 34,4% menjadi Rp1,08 triliun. Neraca BSSR juga relatif kuat dengan tidak adanya utang berbunga material dalam laporan tersebut.

Dengan kondisi tersebut, prospek BSSR setelah pembagian dividen masih berkaitan dengan harga dan volume produksi batubara serta kemampuan perseroan menjaga margin. Namun, investor tetap perlu mengantisipasi volatilitas harga komoditas karena bisnis BSSR bersifat siklikal.

KKGI juga dinilai memiliki daya tarik dari sisi arus kas dan posisi neraca yang relatif konservatif. Pada semester I 2026, pendapatan KKGI naik 4,6% menjadi Rp1,21 triliun dan laba bersih meningkat 122,2% menjadi Rp37,1 miliar.

Meski demikian, profitabilitas KKGI masih lebih kecil dibandingkan BSSR. Karena itu, keberlanjutan dividend yield tinggi akan sangat bergantung pada kinerja operasional dan kondisi harga batubara.

"KKGI lebih tepat dilihat sebagai kombinasi antara dividend play dan exposure terhadap siklus komoditas," ujar Nafan.

Sementara itu, HEXA memiliki karakter bisnis yang lebih terkait dengan alat berat dan aktivitas pertambangan sehingga prospeknya tetap sensitif terhadap siklus belanja modal pertambangan. Dividen sebesar US$0,013319 per saham memberikan yield sekitar 5,9% berdasarkan harga sekitar Rp4.040 per saham.

Namun, investor perlu mencermati payout ratio HEXA yang relatif tinggi.Sustainabilitydividen perlu dibandingkan dengan kemampuan perseroan menghasilkanfree cash flowdan laba ke depan.

VICO memiliki valuasiprice to book value(PBV) yang relatif rendah, tetapi struktur neracanya perlu dicermati karena leverage cukup tinggi. Pada semester I 2026, laba bersih VICO sekitar Rp100,4 miliar, jauh lebih rendah dibandingkan capaian semester I 2025 yang sekitar Rp425,9 miliar.

Dengan demikian, meski dividend yield VICO sekitar 4,6%, investor perlu melihat apakah penurunan laba tersebut bersifat sementara atau mencerminkan normalisasi kinerja yang lebih struktural.

Untuk IFII, dividend yield sekitar 2,3%. Fundamental perseroan relatif lebih defensif dari sisi struktur utang, tetapi kinerja semester I 2026 mengalami pelemahan. Pendapatan turun 12% menjadi Rp612 miliar dan laba bersih turun 28,3% menjadi Rp78,1 miliar.

"Daya tarik IFII lebih bergantung pada potensi pemulihan permintaan dan margin bisnis fibreboard daripada semata-mata dividen interim Rp5 per saham," kata Nafan.

Sementara itu, CDIA memiliki dividend yield paling rendah di antara keenam saham tersebut, yakni sekitar 0,2%. Karena itu, Nafan menilai CDIA kurang tepat jika dibeli hanya untuk mengejar dividen.

Dividen interim Rp1,42 per saham lebih mencerminkan distribusi kas kepada pemegang saham dibandingkan menjadi dividend play dengan yield tinggi. Apalagi, valuasi CDIA masih relatif tinggi dan perusahaan membutuhkan belanja modal besar untuk ekspansi infrastruktur.

Menurut Nafan, katalis CDIA setelah pembagian dividen lebih berkaitan dengan pertumbuhan bisnis, ekspansi aset, dan kemampuan menghasilkan arus kas dari proyek-proyek infrastrukturnya.

"CDIA rekomendasinya adalahwait and see," ujar Nafan.

Sementara itu, Senior Equity Research Analyst Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia, Sukarno Alatas, mengatakan BSSR menawarkan dividend yield sekitar 7,4%, disusul KKGI sekitar 6,1% dan HEXA sekitar 5,8%.

Meski demikian, yield tinggi tetap perlu dilihat bersama potensi koreksi harga saat ex-date. Menurut Sukarno, BSSR juga perlu dicermati karena harga sahamnya telah naik cukup signifikan menjelang cum date sehingga risiko dividend trap perlu diperhatikan.

Investor, kata Sukarno, sebaiknya tidak hanya mengejar dividen, tetapi menghitung total return dari kombinasi dividen dan potensi perubahan harga saham.

"Dividend capture dapat dilakukan dengan membeli sebelum cum date dan menjual setelah ex-date, tetapi risikonya adalah koreksi harga melebihi nilai dividen," jelas Sukarno.

Alternatif yang lebih konservatif, lanjut dia, adalah menunggu tekanan harga setelah ex-date dan masuk kembali apabila fundamental emiten masih mendukung.

Sukarno menilai BSSR dan KKGI relatif menarik untuk dicermati karena didukung bisnis batubara dan kemampuan menghasilkan kas, meski keduanya tetap sensitif terhadap harga komoditas. KKGI juga memiliki tambahan daya tarik dari posisi kas yang kuat dan leverage rendah.

HEXA menawarkan yield tinggi, tetapi investor perlu mencermati tren laba yang masih tertekan. VICO memiliki yield sekitar 4,6%, namun kinerja labanya lebih fluktuatif

Sementara itu, IFII memiliki yield lebih rendah sekitar 2,3% dengan fokus pada potensi pemulihan earnings. Adapun CDIA kurang menarik sebagai dividend play karena yield hanya sekitar 0,2% dan valuasinya relatif tinggi.

Untuk strategi berbasis dividen, Sukarno menyebut BSSR, KKGI, dan HEXA menjadi tiga emiten yang layak dicermati, dengan karakter yang berbeda. BSSR memiliki dividend yield tinggi, KKGI menawarkan kombinasi yield dan neraca yang relatif sehat, sedangkan HEXA lebih bergantung pada pemulihan siklus bisnis alat berat.

Investor tetap perlu mempertimbangkan harga masuk dan potensi koreksi setelah ex-date, bukan hanya besaran dividen.

Adapun KKGI membagikan dividen Rp20 per saham dengan cum dividen pasar reguler pada 23 September 2026 dan pembayaran pada 15 Oktober 2026. HEXA membagikan dividen US$0,013319 per saham dengan cum dividen pada 25 September 2026 dan pembayaran pada 21 Oktober 2026.

VICO dan IFII sama-sama memiliki cum dividen pasar reguler pada 28 September 2026. VICO membagikan Rp8 per saham dengan pembayaran 22 Oktober 2026, sedangkan IFII membagikan dividen interim Rp5 per saham dengan pembayaran 15 Oktober 2026.

Selanjutnya, BSSR membagikan dividen interim Rp406,16 per saham dengan cum dividen pada 29 September 2026 dan pembayaran 9 Oktober 2026. CDIA membagikan dividen interim Rp1,42 per saham dengan total US$10 juta.

title: Rupiah Mulai Konsolidasi Usai Melemah 9 Hari, Ini Proyeksi hingga Akhir 2026
article:
Reporter:Yasmine Awalia| Editor:Yudho Winarto

KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA.Pergerakan rupiah masih menjadi perhatian pasar setelah mencatat pelemahan selama sembilan hari berturut-turut. Namun, mata uang Garuda mulai menunjukkan penguatan pada perdagangan Rabu (23/9/2026).

Rupiah spot ditutup di level Rp 17.818 per dolar Amerika Serikat (AS), menguat 0,37% dibandingkan posisi sehari sebelumnya yang berada di Rp 17.884 per dolar AS.

Penguatan tersebut terjadi setelah Bank Indonesia (BI) memutuskan mempertahankan suku bunga acuan atau BI-Rate di level 5,75% dalam Rapat Dewan Gubernur (RDG) pada 22-23 September 2026.

Selain BI-Rate, BI mempertahankan suku bunga Deposit Facility sebesar 4,75% dan Lending Facility di level 6,50%.

BI menyatakan, keputusan tersebut ditempuh dengan mempertimbangkan stabilitas nilai tukar rupiah yang masih dapat dijaga, sekaligus mendukung pertumbuhan ekonomi dan pengendalian inflasi.

Di tengah tekanan terhadap rupiah, BI juga akan memperkuat kebijakan insentif untuk menarik aliran modal asing.

Bank sentral akan mengoptimalkan instrumen moneter untuk menjaga stabilitas nilai tukar, sekaligus mempercepat pendalaman pasar uang dan pasar valuta asing.

Pengamat mata uang dan komoditas Ibrahim Assuaibi menilai tekanan terhadap rupiah masih cukup besar.

Penguatan indeks dolar AS, sikap hawkish sejumlah pejabat The Fed, harga minyak yang tinggi, serta ketidakpastian geopolitik menjadi sejumlah faktor yang perlu dicermati pasar.

Untuk perdagangan berikutnya, Ibrahim memperkirakan rupiah bergerak fluktuatif dengan kecenderungan melemah di kisaran Rp 17.810-Rp 17.860 per dolar AS.

Sementara itu, Chief Analyst Doo Financial Futures Lukman Leong melihat pelemahan rupiah dalam beberapa waktu terakhir merupakan kombinasi dari sejumlah faktor eksternal.

Selain penguatan dolar AS, tingginya imbal hasil US Treasury, harga minyak yang masih tinggi dan ketidakpastian geopolitik turut memberikan tekanan.

Meski demikian, setelah melemah cukup panjang, rupiah dinilai mulai memasuki fase konsolidasi.

"Dalam jangka pendek rupiah masih volatil, tetapi ruang pelemahan mulai lebih terbatas jika tekanan global tidak kembali meningkat," ujar Lukman.

Menurut Lukman, risiko rupiah kembali menuju level Rp 18.000 per dolar AS masih terbuka. Skenario tersebut dapat terjadi apabila The Fed kembali memberikan sinyal hawkish, imbal hasil US Treasury meningkat, harga minyak kembali naik atau terjadi eskalasi geopolitik.

Namun, level Rp 18.000 dinilai sebagai level psikologis yang kuat. Karena itu, diperlukan tekanan eksternal yang cukup besar agar rupiah dapat menembus sekaligus bertahan di atas level tersebut.

Untuk akhir 2026, Lukman memperkirakan rupiah berada dalam kisaran Rp 17.500-Rp 18.000 per dolar AS.

Jika harga minyak turun dan imbal hasil obligasi AS melandai, rupiah berpeluang bergerak menuju sisi bawah kisaran tersebut.

Sebaliknya, peningkatan kembali tekanan eksternal dapat mendorong rupiah mendekati level Rp 18.000 per dolar AS.

title: Impor Emas China Tembus 1.000 Ton, Prospek Harga Emas Kembali Terangkat
article:
Reporter:Vivit Dewi| Editor:Tri Sulistiowati

KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA.Harga emas masih bergerak volatil di tengah tekanan dolar AS dan ekspektasi kebijakan suku bunga The Fed. Namun, kuatnya permintaan dari China menjadi salah satu sentimen yang menopang harga emas.

Berdasarkan data Trading Economics pada Rabu (23/9) pukul 17.20 WIB, harga emas spot berada di level US$ 4.316 per ons troi. Harga tersebut turun 1,10% dalam sehari dan 7,37% dalam sebulan, namun masih menguat 1,07% dalam sepekan.

Di sisi lain, impor emas China hingga Agustus telah melampaui 1.000 ton, bahkan melebihi total impor sepanjang 2025. Kondisi tersebut mencerminkan masih kuatnya permintaan investasi emas di China dan menjadi sentimen positif bagi pasar emas.

Analis PT Finex Bisnis Solusi Futures, Brahmantya Himawan menilai kuatnya pembelian emas dari China, baik oleh bank sentral maupun investor, masih menjadi salah satu penopang harga emas dalam jangka menengah hingga panjang.

"Pembelian bank sentral dan investor China menjadi salah satu faktor yang dapat menjaga dasar harga emas dalam jangka menengah-panjang," kata Brahmantya kepada Kontan, Rabu (23/9/2026).

Selain impor yang tinggi, permintaan emas China juga ditopang oleh pembelian bank sentral dan investor domestik. People’s Bank of China (PBoC) masih melanjutkan akumulasi emas, sementara ETF emas China turut menunjukkan permintaan investasi.

Sementara itu, Analis Komoditas sekaligus Founder Traderindo.com, Wahyu Laksono mengatakan, China memiliki peranan penting sebagai salah satu jangkar permintaan emas global, baik melalui pembelian PBoC maupun permintaan dari investor dan masyarakat ritel.

"China, baik melalui People’s Bank of China (PBoC) maupun sektor ritel/investasi domestik, memegang peranan krusial sebagai jangkar permintaan global," ujar Wahyu.

Kuatnya permintaan China tersebut dapat menjadi bantalan bagi harga emas ketika pasar menghadapi tekanan dari dolar AS dan kebijakan suku bunga.

Di sisi lain, penurunan harga minyak dan imbal hasil obligasi AS dapat menjadi katalis positif bagi emas apabila berlanjut, karena berpotensi meredakan tekanan inflasi dan mengurangi ekspektasi kenaikan suku bunga.

Hingga akhir 2026, Wahyu memperkirakan harga emas masih berpotensi bergerak dalam rentang US$ 4.300-US$ 5.000 per ons troi.

Dalam skenario moderat, harga emas berada di sekitar US$ 4.500, sedangkan apabila inflasi mereda dan kondisi geopolitik relatif stabil, harga berpeluang menuju US$ 4.800-US$ 4.900.

Sementara itu, Brahmantya memproyeksikan harga emas dapat mencapai US$ 4.800-US$ 5.000 per ons troi pada akhir 2026 apabila area support US$ 4.200-US$ 3.900 tetap bertahan.

Prospek tersebut akan semakin kuat apabila pembelian emas oleh bank sentral dan investor China tetap tinggi, sementara tekanan dari dolar AS dan ekspektasi kenaikan suku bunga mulai mereda.

title: Kinerja Positif, Tapi Pergerakan Saham ADMR Masih Terbatas
article:
Reporter:Yuliana Hema| Editor:Tri Sulistiowati

KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA.Saham PT Alamtri Minerals Indonesia Tbk (ADMR) masih bergerak terbatas. Padahal entitas Grup Alamtri ini membukukan kinerja keuangan yang positif didorong kenaikan harga komoditas.

Pada perdagangan Rabu (23/9), saham ADMR mulai menguat 2,63% ke Rp 1.560 per saham. Sepanjang tahun berjalan ini, saham ADMR tak bergerak kemana-mana alias flat.

Senior Market Analyst Mirae Asset Sekuritas Nafan Aji Gusta menilai fundamental ADMR masih menarik. Namun, pasar membutuhkan bukti lebih kuat bahwa ekspansi aluminium mampu mengkompensasi volatilitas bisnis batubara metalurgi.

“ADMR tetap memiliki fundamental yang menarik, tetapi pasar saat ini masih membutuhkan bukti lebih kuat bahwa ekspansi aluminium dapat segera mengompensasi volatilitas bisnis batubara metalurgi,” katanya kepada Kontan, Rabu (23/9).

Menurut Nafan, pertumbuhan laba ADMR yang solid belum otomatis mendorong rerating harga saham. Dia bilang ekspektasi pasar terhadap ADMR sudah cukup tinggi sehingga investor membutuhkan katalis baru untuk memberikan valuasi lebih tinggi.

Selain itu, kata Nafan, risiko operasional jangka pendek turut menahan pergerakan saham ADMR. Salah satunya adalah gangguan pengiriman batubara kokas akibat rendahnya permukaan Sungai Barito pada musim kering yang membatasi aktivitas pengangkutan.

Setali tiga uang, Research Analyst Phintraco Sekuritas Vinna N. Rachmawati menyebut kondisi kekeringan berkepanjangan berpotensi membebani operasional ADMR pada kuartal mendatang, meski terdapat katalis dari bisnis aluminium.

“Akibatnya, kegiatan logistik di sepanjang Sungai Barito untuk sementara dihentikan dan batubara ditumpuk di area pelabuhan ADMR,” tulisnya Vinna dalam riset yang dirilis pada Senin (21/9).

Vinna menyebut sebenarnya kinerja operasional ADMR pada semester pertama 2026 sebenarnya cukup solid. Volume penjualan batubara metalurgi meningkat 9% secara tahunan, seiring harga jual rata-rata yang lebih tinggi.

Pendapatan ADMR pada semester pertama 2026 mencapai US$ 584 juta, naik 39,3% secara tahunan atauYear on Year(YoY). Segmen penjualan produk pertambangan menyumbang US$582 juta atau sekitar 99,6% dari total pendapatan.

Laba kotor ADMR juga meningkat 54,2% YoY menjadi US$ 227,8 juta, dengan margin laba kotor melebar menjadi 47,6%. Laba bersih meningkat 24% YoY menjadi US$ 174,2 juta per Juni 2026 dibandingkan US$ 140,5 juta.

Namun, kontribusi bisnis aluminium belum masuk ke laporan pendapatan ADMR pada semester pertama 2026. Melalui PT Kalimantan Aluminium Industry, smelter aluminium kini berada dalam tahap peningkatan produksi atau ramp-up.

Vinna memperkirakan ADMR mulai membukukan pendapatan dari penjualan aluminium pada semester kedua 2026. Tahap pertama smelter tersebut ditargetkan mencapai kapasitas penuh sebesar 500.000 ton pada akhir tahun.

Masuknya kontribusi aluminium menjadi salah satu katalis yang dinilai dapat mengubah persepsi pasar terhadap ADMR. Menurutnya, investor berpotensi mulai menilai ADMR sebagai perusahaan mineral  dengan eksposur aluminium, bukan hanya produsen batubara kokas.

Di sisi komoditas, Vinna melihat prospek aluminium domestik masih positif. Kapasitas aluminium primer Indonesia diproyeksikan meningkat hampir 11 kali lipat menjadi 10,4 juta ton pada 2030 dari 850.000 ton pada 2025.

Konsumsi aluminium domestik juga diperkirakan tumbuh 14% pada 2026 dan sekitar 16% secaracompound annual growth ratepada 2027–2030. Vinna bilang pertumbuhan tersebut didukung industrialisasi, pembangunan infrastruktur dan kebijakan industri.

"Segmen aluminium dapat menjadi katalis pertumbuhan utama ADMR. Kontribusi bisnis tersebut juga diproyeksikan secara bertahap menjadi sumber pendapatan yang semakin signifikan," jelasnya.

Di sisi lain, Phintraco Sekuritas tetap melihat ada risiko membayangi prospek ADMR. Selain gangguan logistik akibat kondisi Sungai Barito, investor perlu mencermati volatilitas harga komoditas energi serta potensi perlambatan permintaan baja global.

Meski begitu, Phintraco Sekuritas masih mempertahankan rekomendasi beli  ADMR dengan target harga di Rp 2.310 per saham. Nafan juga merekomendasikan beli ADMR dengan area masuk di Rp 1.505–Rp 1.595.

title: ASII Siapkan Investasi Besar di Tiga Bisnis Inti, Ini Prospek Sahamnya
article:
Reporter:Rashif Usman| Editor:Handoyo

KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA. PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) akan mempertahankan fokus investasinya pada tiga lini bisnis utama hingga 2027. Ketiga bisnis tersebut mencakup otomotif, jasa keuangan, serta solusi pertambangan dan alat berat.

Strategi tersebut menjadi bagian dari upaya Astra menjaga pertumbuhan bisnis sekaligus mengoptimalkan alokasi modal. Pasalnya, ketiga lini bisnis tersebut berkontribusi sekitar 90% terhadap total laba Astra International.

Head of Corporate Investor Relations Astra International, Tira Ardianti mengatakan, sejalan dengan fokus bisnis tersebut, alokasi belanja modal dan investasi perseroan juga akan diprioritaskan pada ketiga bisnis inti tersebut.

Salah satu langkah konkret yang mencerminkan strategi tersebut adalah rencana Astra menambah kepemilikan saham di PT Astra Otoparts Tbk (AUTO) melalui skema Voluntary Tender Offer (VTO), dengan harga penawaran Rp3.600 per saham. Apabila seluruh target saham dapat diperoleh, transaksi tersebut membutuhkan dana sekitar Rp858 miliar.

Langkah tersebut sejalan dengan fokus perseroan memperkuat tiga bisnis inti, khususnya sektor otomotif melalui penguatan bisnis komponen.

"Ini contoh konkrit Astra fokus pada bisnis inti. Astra melakukan investasi, dengan mengutamakan bisnis yang memiliki strategic fit dengan Astra, dan mampu menghasilkan tingkat pengembalian yang baik, serta dapat memperkuat ekosistem Astra," kata Tira di Jakarta, Rabu (23/9/2026).

Meski demikian, Astra tetap membuka peluang investasi di luar bisnis inti atau wider businesses selama peluang tersebut memenuhi kriteria investasi yang telah ditetapkan perusahaan.

Tira menegaskan, investasi pada portofolio di luar bisnis inti diperkirakan tidak akan dilakukan dalam skala besar. Adapun nilai pasti investasi pada segmen tersebut belum dapat disampaikan karena masih dalam tahap pembahasan dan evaluasi internal.Prospek Astra

Analis sekaligus Branch Manager Panin Sekuritas Pondok Indah Elandry Pratama mengatakan, fokus ASII pada sektor otomotif, jasa keuangan, serta solusi pertambangan dan alat berat cukup logis untuk memperkuat alokasi modal. Pasalnya, ketiga lini tersebut selama ini menjadi mesin utama laba grup.

"Strategi ini juga bisa membuat belanja modal lebih disiplin dan diarahkan ke bisnis yang sudah memiliki skala, ekosistem, serta competitive advantage yang kuat," ucap Elandry kepada Kontan, Rabu (23/9/2026).

Namun, Elandry menilai tantangan Astra adalah karakter tiga bisnis tersebut yang masih cukup siklikal. Karena itu, keberhasilan strategi hingga 2027 akan sangat bergantung pada kemampuan Astra menjaga keseimbangan kontribusi antarsegmen.

Pada semester I-2026, misalnya, laba dari bisnis otomotif masih tumbuh 9% dan jasa keuangan meningkat 6%. Namun, laba dari solusi pertambangan dan alat berat justru turun 46%.

Kondisi tersebut menunjukkan pentingnya diversifikasi di antara tiga bisnis inti Astra untuk membantu meredam dampak siklus pada masing-masing sektor.

Ke depan, sejumlah sentimen positif berpotensi mendukung kinerja Astra, antara lain pemulihan penjualan kendaraan, perbaikan daya beli masyarakat, pertumbuhan pembiayaan Astra Financial, serta normalisasi aktivitas pertambangan dan alat berat.

Penjualan mobil Astra pada semester I-2026 tercatat tumbuh 10% secara tahunan. Di sisi lain, bisnis jasa keuangan masih mampu mencatat pertumbuhan laba.

Rencana share buyback ASII hingga Rp8 triliun juga menjadi tambahan sentimen positif dari sisi shareholder return.

Meski demikian, investor tetap perlu mencermati sejumlah risiko. Beberapa di antaranya adalah pelemahan daya beli, persaingan di industri otomotif terutama dengan masuknya merek baru dan kendaraan listrik, dampak suku bunga terhadap pembiayaan, serta volatilitas harga komoditas dan kebijakan pertambangan.

Risiko tersebut telah terlihat pada semester I-2026. Laba bersih ASII turun 19% menjadi Rp12,5 triliun, terutama dipengaruhi melemahnya kontribusi bisnis pertambangan dan alat berat serta adanya non-recurring items.

Dari sisi prospek saham, Elandry masih melihat peluang positif bagi ASII dalam jangka menengah hingga panjang, terutama apabila pemulihan sektor otomotif berlanjut dan kontribusi bisnis pertambangan kembali normal.

Menurut Elandry, fokus Astra pada tiga bisnis inti berpotensi membuat penggunaan modal menjadi lebih efisien. Kebijakan buyback juga dapat memberikan dukungan terhadap shareholder return.

Namun, investor tetap perlu memperhatikan proses pemulihan laba karena kinerja ASII pada semester I-2026 belum sepenuhnya kuat.

Secara valuasi, Elandry menilai saham ASII masih menarik untuk strategi akumulasi atau buy on weakness, dengan target harga di kisaran Rp7.000-Rp7.300.

"Katalis menuju target tersebut terutama berasal dari recovery otomotif, pertumbuhan jasa keuangan, normalisasi bisnis alat berat dan pertambangan, serta disiplin capital allocation. Risiko utamanya tetap pelemahan konsumsi dan recovery sektor pertambangan yang lebih lambat dari perkiraan," tutupnya.
